en.headline: Natalie Kan takes Asian Games 100m butterfly bronze and Hong Kong record
en.dek: The 24-year-old finished third in 58.05 seconds in Tokyo, breaking Siobhan Haughey’s previous Hong Kong mark of 58.12 set in 2023.
body: Hong Kong swimmer Natalie Kan claimed bronze in the women’s 100-metre butterfly at the Asian Games on Wednesday, posting 58.05 seconds at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre and breaking the Hong Kong record previously held by Siobhan Haughey.

China’s Yu Yiting took gold in 56.41 seconds, with teammate Zhang Yufei second in 56.44. Kan powered past South Korea’s An Se Hyeon in the final 50 metres to secure the final podium place. Fellow Hong Kong swimmer Yeung Hoi-ching finished ninth in 1:00.55.

It was Kan’s first individual medal at the continental Games. After the race she said the result had come as a surprise and that she would process it overnight, adding that the Hong Kong record showed she could keep improving.

zh.headline: 簡綽桐亞運100米蝶泳摘銅兼破港績
zh.dek: 24歲港將周三在東京以58秒05奪銅，打破何詩蓓2023年所創58秒12的香港紀錄。
body: 香港泳手簡綽桐周三在亞運女子100米蝶泳決賽以58秒05奪得銅牌，並打破何詩蓓保持的香港紀錄。
中國隊余依婷以56秒41奪金，張雨霏56秒44獲銀。簡綽桐在後半程超越南韓安世賢，鎖定第三名。另一港將楊凱晴以1分00秒55排第九。
這是簡綽桐首面亞運個人獎牌。賽後她表示成績出乎意料，需要時間消化，並指破港績證明自己仍有進步空間。
